Educor crisis

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Educor proud history of independent colleges has collapsed- what now for the students desperate for a decent qualification

Unique Selling Point:
Finally the Department of Education has taken action against Educor, deregistering City Varsity, Damelin, ICESA and Lyceum College. For the last couple of years these institutions have been in financial trouble, but they failed to submit the 2021/2022 Financial records and Tax Clearance certificates to the Department of Education and despite being given several extensions they failed to comply. They lied about their student numbers, saying they had 50 000 students when records show closer to 13 000 and the quality of the education is below standard and does not comply with the CITA regulations. Students are getting marks based on attendance rather than exams. The staff turnover is extremely high due to salaries not being paid. Electricity and rental bills are not paid and Braamfontein campus was simply closed without notice to staff or students.

Summary:
The Education Department informed Educor at the end of last year that they were not allowed to register new students in 2024 until they complied. But despite this very public announcement covered by all the major TV stations City Varsity in Cape Town is in denial. Last week they told staff and lecturers it was business as usual, and the media had got it all wrong.
What now for the staff and lecturers who have been struggling with the collapsing college? The Education Department have given them till the end of 2025 to complete the 2nd and 3rd year course. But the state of the facilities and already in a dire situation.
Ashton Solomon senior lecture in Multimedia Digital design from 2019 has seen it all, he resigned last week when City Varsity blatantly lied to students. He will speak to the appalling situation of having to work for weeks without electricity due to unpaid bills. Students being admitted to courses they were clearly not qualified to take simply to bring in fees. Computer equipment that does not work and 15 students sharing the few computers that do work. He recorded the zoom meeting where staff discussed passing students on attendance rather than exam results and where the senior lecturer was fired when he opposed this. He will also speak to the fact that the staff are not paid, and do not receive support from the academic management and are expected to string students along.
“Acting for Camera” is one of the courses on offer at City Varsity and will set you back R48,000. Irate 3rd year student Billy Shumba Brighton says it’s false advertising. He was promised he would ”experience meaningful mentorship by the best academics in the industry who keep close ties to their field of focus. Our students’ learning experience is enhanced by state-of-the-art equipment and facilities. Boasting studios, an infinity wall, dark room, casting rooms and fully equipped labs, our campus is sure to give you that VIP experience.“
There was no camera to act in front of, for most of his 1st year, they had to use the lecturers’ cell phones and their own cell phones to do their final assessments, says Billy. They had a great lecturer for a couple months, but he was never paid so he left and so there was no end-of-year performance, the students filmed their own final performance and the lecturer returned briefly to assess their submissions. Now there is one dysfunctional camera instead of acting in front of 3 cameras. So many lecturers left during the year that they felt completely demoralized. Exams are required to have external examiners, but City Varsity is known for not paying, so now there are no independent assessments done. Billy’s mother is a domestic worker and he can’t face telling her about the shocking state of the course, and now the news that City Varsity has been deregistered he fears that his qualification is worth nothing.
Mazwaneni Fani is a first year student, he paid he registration fee and a pre assessment fee to get into the Multi media course. His mother is a nurse and extremely distressed at the situation and says Mazwaneni mental state is really bad since the announcement – he was so exited to get into City Varsity because last year he didn’t qualify for any of the technical colleges. She is unable to get any answers out of City varsity and simply referred to Damlin College, which has also been deregistered. She will make an very strong interview.



Further information:
I am hoping to secure an interview with a student to transferred from Braamfontein college who now faces closure of the CT campus and the way EDUCOR has handled the whole affair.

Script:


Opening sequence of Ashton on the beach throwing ball for his dog
VO: One of the perks of Ashton Solomon’s new life
For the last 3 years he’s been lecturer, at City Varsity in Cape Town.
Ashton: I enjoy the students and I enjoyed like being able to share the skill and the craft …seeing them grow and going from barely switching on a computer to being like legit.

Visuals : Sinqobile walking up the stairs into his bedroom
New to Cape Town - Sinqobile Mdingazwe is a 3rd year Acting before Camera student - at City Varsity.
Sinqobile: One of my dreams is to actually, uh, participate in changing the film industry in South Africa, …., because South Africa is a country with a lot of cultures, a lot of languages, and a magnitude of stories to be told

VO: City Varsity is a private higher education college offering courses in the creative arts, acting for camera, film making, photography and multimedia digital design. It’s owned by Educor Holdings - which manages 7 different educational brands

VO: Last month - the Minister of Higher Education Blade Nzimande - announced the deregistration of City Varsity, Damelin College, Icesa City Campus and Lyceum college, impacting 60 Educor institutions across the country

BLADE 8.26 In addition to failing to submit evidence of their financial viability to the Department the four Educor brands can be deemed as dysfunctional

VO: It’s a tragic demise- Educor is the largest private higher education institution in Southern Africa - and used to have - an excellent reputation.

LINK: So many young lives filled with ambition and dreams of big futures were crushed when the news broke, but the situation has been dire for quite some time

VO: Sinqobile did his first two years at the Braamfontein City Varsity campus in Johannesburg
Sinquobile “ We're acting students, we need to have cameras to shoot but we didn't have those cameras. We didn't have a lot of equipment. We didn't have props, mics, - then the lectures started telling us that there's been a problem at City Varsity, it's just that …..They were not allowed to talk about it.

VO: The situation in Cape Town wasn’t much better. This student fears revealing his identity - will ruin his future.

Billy “gradually a couple of lecturers started leaving, they weren't getting paid for like months. The lecturers have lost their cars , couldn't pay rent, had mental breakdowns in front of our face because their own needs weren't being met, you know, how can you survive without money, you can't survive without money?

Ashton:…. we were complaining about being getting paid late and then they would be like, hey, don't don't say anything in the WhatsApp groups. ….me and a lot of the staff that I spoke to, didn't feel safe, to kind of just voice your opinions at the end of the day

VO: There is a striking culture of fear and distrust. After what some acting students told us, weeks went by without lecturers, and with little or no equipment, students demanded a meeting with Educor - they got nothing but promises.
Sinquobile “The day came where they were supposed to deliver what they promised. And they did not respond. They did not say anything. We started striking again,actually cleared out the building from the eighth floor down to the ground.

Billy They would literally say if anything is happening wrong on campus, you can sue us. - the person that we saw who was the representative in the face of Educor, she's gone, you know? So. So make it make sense you know

VO: Carte Blanche was sent a recorded Teams meeting in which the assessments were discussed among lecturers. During the conversation - a bizarre solution - is put forward

” I asked and he says I can take attendance as assessment marks”

VO: In other words, a student's record in attending class - would count towards their academic marks.

Ashton - It's fine you can't take attendance as a mark, which is like nuts because like, basically you just show up and you pass which is crazy.

VO: In Johannesburg after months of late payments lecturers were facing Christmas - still without pay.

VO: This voice note from a lecturer explains that the grades students received, were not based on the marked exams scripts - as they were withholding them - as a kind of leverage in their pay dispute.

VOICE NOTE… 1.05 They cooked your marks, yes they cooked your marks yes they gave you marks that we don’t know as lecturers

LINK: When the Department of Higher Education announced the deregistration the head of City Varsity in Cape Town told the students nothing had changed - the media had got it all wrong.
Billy : And then he says, I have a list from the Department of Higher Education and training themselves that clearly states that our campus is still registered. That list was dated August of 2023.

VO In other words - he was using a list 7 months older - than the one released by the Minister

“I went on to the the website of the Department of Higher Education and Training and I downloaded the latest list 17th of March 2024, which clearly states institutions that are deregistered and City Varsity was there

Lourensa”: Was it ever a moment where you considered walking away from city varsity?

Billy “What would it mean for my mother paying all that money? And now I'm walking away without having finished what I started.We don't have that sort of economical means to just up and leave and go to another institution and start all over again.

VO: His mother paid close to R200 000 for his studies.

Students fear that the campus in Cape Town - could just be shut down without warning - like what happened to Braamfontein City Varsity earlier this year.

Sinqobile “They sent messages to our parents. That campus is still being fumigated. And then they dropped the bomb on us in February. And then they said they were closing down. So when they shut down the building, they gave us the list of institutions that we can transfer to….. When we actually went to those institutions. Those institutions said, we know nothing about this because City Varsity and Educor hasn't communicated anything with us

VO: Sinqobile managed to transfer to Cape Town City Varsity - but is taking enormous strain after this announcement.

He lives in this windowless, cockroach infested room.

It costs him - 5-thousand-rand-a-month.

Upsound with Lourensa and Ashton looking at students work

VO: The battles with management eventually wore Ashton down - the reward of seeing students develop - was no longer enough

Lourensa: And now you decided to resign?

Ashton: I couldn't sit there and pretend that everything's fine with the students. Um. And then just continue like nothing's wrong. Where as you messing with young people's lives, ……you're ruining people that might have had potential.

Link: We have tried to get some straight answers from Educor about what the future holds for these students, but like them we have hit a blank wall.
Voice recording. Can I just ask you a few questions about the status of City Varsity in Cape Town and the students that are currently registered.
Mam could you put it in an email.
VO And as for answers about the management
10.28 Could you please just tell me who is the CEO of Educor- Mam put it in writing and I will revert back to you- .It's very peculiar behaviour, umhum
VO: The identity of the Educor CEO - remains a mystery.
In its statement Educor says it is appealing the deregistration. They commit to the long-term operation of the Cape Town campus - and say Braamfontein campus students were relocated to comparable institutions. They claim - all City Varsity qualifications remain accredited by the Council of Higher Education.
LINK: What so distressing about all this is that the students and their parents are the real victims in this whole saga. Will their qualifications be worth the paper they are written on? Will Educor reimbursed them? Their track record of paying their bills is atrocious and their academic credibility in shreds
Billy -The only relief we ever got was from the minister himself of higher education and training, when he said that our degrees are still valid.

Lourensa : But are you confident that it will be valid? the diploma you will get at the end of the course

Billy” The only thing that makes me confident is that the minister himself said that and not Eudcor

Sinqobile “The industry is not going to view City Varsity students the same. ….I'm afraid that many other institutions will not recognize my degree

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Finally the Department of Education has taken action against Educor, deregistering City Varsity, Damelin, ICESA and Lyceum College. For the last couple of years these institutions have been in financial trouble, but they failed to submit the 2021/2022 Financial records and Tax Clearance certificates to the Department of Education and despite being given several extensions they failed to comply. They lied about their student numbers, saying they had 50 000 students when records show closer to 13 000 and the quality of the education is below standard and does not comply with the CITA regulations. Students are getting marks based on attendance rather than exams. The staff turnover is extremely high due to salaries not being paid. Electricity and rental bills are not paid and Braamfontein campus was simply closed without notice to staff or students.
metadata.Summary: The Education Department informed Educor at the end of last year that they were not allowed to register new students in 2024 until they complied. But despite this very public announcement covered by all the major TV stations City Varsity in Cape Town is in denial. Last week they told staff and lecturers it was business as usual, and the media had got it all wrong. What now for the staff and lecturers who have been struggling with the collapsing college? The Education Department have given them till the end of 2025 to complete the 2nd and 3rd year course. But the state of the facilities and already in a dire situation. Ashton Solomon senior lecture in Multimedia Digital design from 2019 has seen it all, he resigned last week when City Varsity blatantly lied to students. He will speak to the appalling situation of having to work for weeks without electricity due to unpaid bills. Students being admitted to courses they were clearly not qualified to take simply to bring in fees. Computer equipment that does not work and 15 students sharing the few computers that do work. He recorded the zoom meeting where staff discussed passing students on attendance rather than exam results and where the senior lecturer was fired when he opposed this. He will also speak to the fact that the staff are not paid, and do not receive support from the academic management and are expected to string students along. “Acting for Camera” is one of the courses on offer at City Varsity and will set you back R48,000. Irate 3rd year student Billy Shumba Brighton says it’s false advertising. He was promised he would ”experience meaningful mentorship by the best academics in the industry who keep close ties to their field of focus. Our students’ learning experience is enhanced by state-of-the-art equipment and facilities. Boasting studios, an infinity wall, dark room, casting rooms and fully equipped labs, our campus is sure to give you that VIP experience.“ There was no camera to act in front of, for most of his 1st year, they had to use the lecturers’ cell phones and their own cell phones to do their final assessments, says Billy. They had a great lecturer for a couple months, but he was never paid so he left and so there was no end-of-year performance, the students filmed their own final performance and the lecturer returned briefly to assess their submissions. Now there is one dysfunctional camera instead of acting in front of 3 cameras. So many lecturers left during the year that they felt completely demoralized. Exams are required to have external examiners, but City Varsity is known for not paying, so now there are no independent assessments done. Billy’s mother is a domestic worker and he can’t face telling her about the shocking state of the course, and now the news that City Varsity has been deregistered he fears that his qualification is worth nothing. Mazwaneni Fani is a first year student, he paid he registration fee and a pre assessment fee to get into the Multi media course. His mother is a nurse and extremely distressed at the situation and says Mazwaneni mental state is really bad since the announcement – he was so exited to get into City Varsity because last year he didn’t qualify for any of the technical colleges. She is unable to get any answers out of City varsity and simply referred to Damlin College, which has also been deregistered. She will make an very strong interview.
